issue.body:
According to the [ASGI 3.0 specification](https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/specs/main.html#applications), Applications can be defined as a single callable accepting `scope`, `receive` and `send`. In contrast, there is a reference to a Legacy Application which is a callable class instantiated with `scope` and called with `receive` and `send`.

According to the release notes documented on the [starlette.io website](https://www.starlette.io/release-notes/), 0.12.0 made Starlette compatible with ASGI 3.0.

However, I am unable to use a sole callable as an Application when adding middleware to Starlette. An example is as follows:
```python
async def hello_world(scope, receive, send):
    logging.info("Hello World!")

app = Starlette()
app.add_middleware(hello_world)
```
This results in the following exception:
```
TypeError: hello_world() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'receive' and 'send'
```
This indicates that it is still using the Legacy Application style for ASGI middleware.

Was this ASGI Application Signature expected to be changed with ASGI 3.0? Is there a technical reason for this style of middleware to continue being used?
issue.title: ASGI 3.0 Application (including Middleware) Signature
